certainty_reasoning: Cook writes 'secretary, companion and possibly also sexual partner', and 'possibly' is doing all the work: no letter, diary, memoir or second witness read here says anything further, and Cook's supporting endnote has not been chased.

disputed.claim: that Henning Nyberg was Charles Ricketts's sexual partner as well as his secretary and companion, from about 1930
disputed.asserted_by: Matt Cook, Queer Domesticities (2014), p. 52, and only in the hedged form 'secretary, companion and possibly also sexual partner'
disputed.disputed_by: Nothing positively contradicts it. No source read affirms it either - the hedge is the whole of the evidence, and Cook himself does not commit.
disputed.grounds: A historian's 'possibly' is not an attestation. The residence, the post, the gramophone and the theatre-going are documented and are not in question; what is unsupported is the step from companion to sexual partner. Cook's endnote 149 would be the place to look next.

summary: After Shannon's 1929 fall left him incapable, the twenty-five-year-old Henning Nyberg moved into Townshend House as Ricketts's secretary and companion, bringing a gramophone; the two went out to the theatre and cinema at least three times a week. Ricketts died in 1931.

sources.quote: Soon after, 25-year-old Henning Nyberg moved in as Ricketts' secretary, companion and possibly also sexual partner. Nyberg brought a gramophone with him to Townshend House, and the pair went out to the theatre and cinema at least three times a week.
sources.context: Matt Cook, Queer Domesticities (2014), ch. 1, on the household after Shannon's 1929 accident. Cook's endnote 149 carries the citation; not chased so far.
sources.supports: A named companion in Ricketts's household in his last years; the sexual element is the historian's hedge, not a finding.
